Harmonized Drug Dataset v3.2 Quality Control

James Bannon, Michael Tran

November 27, 2026

1 Overview

This report is a quality control walkthrough for the lab-generated Harmonized Drug Dataset stored as a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE). The dataset harmonizes multiple drug-related assays and features across a shared compound universe keyed by HDD.Compound.ID so downstream analyses can operate on a consistent sample space. Pubchem.CID is retained when available, but it is not required for a compound to be included.

1.1 Data Sources

This report describes the HDD object and its compound annotations, assays and features. Key sources include:

  • Tox21: NCATS 2014 Challenge training archive, matched by unique full InChIKey. Discordant calls are set to missing for that compound and assay.
  • DeepChem BBBP: retained as blood–brain barrier permeability metadata in colData, not as a separate assay.
  • JUMP-CP membership and source identifiers from the curated cpg0016 MAE.
  • OASIS membership and source identifiers from the curated cpg0037 MAE.
  • GEOM membership and source identifiers from the curated GEOM MAE.
  • LINCS membership and source identifiers from the curated LINCS MAE.
  • CTRPv2 membership and master compound identifiers from the CTRPv2 PharmacoSet.
  • NCI60 membership and NSC identifiers from the NCI60-2026 PharmacoSet.
  • Bioassays: pulled from AnnotationDB alongside compound metadata, with bioassays filtered to gold-standard assays.
  • Drug indications: ChEMBL indication records pulled from AnnotationDB and stored as a long table in MAE metadata rather than flattened into colData.
  • ATC codes: pulled from AnnotationDB when an authorization key is available.
  • LTKB: DILI labels pulled from AnnotationDB for the LTKB Benchmark Dataset, DILIrank, and DILIst label sets.
  • LiverTox: hepatotoxicity likelihood score and reason pulled from AnnotationDB.
  • DIRIL and DICT: renal and cardiac toxicity labels pulled from AnnotationDB.
  • DailyMed: selected product labels supplied by AnnotationDB, including boxed warnings, warnings/precautions and adverse reactions.
  • Fingerprints: RDKit Morgan count fingerprints generated for compounds with parseable SMILES.

## A MultiAssayExperiment object of 6 listed
##  experiments with user-defined names and respective classes.

##  [2] Tox21: SummarizedExperiment with 12 rows and 6134 columns
##  [3] fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024: SummarizedExperiment with 1024 rows and 646039 columns
##  [4] fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048: SummarizedExperiment with 2048 rows and 646039 columns
##  [5] fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024: SummarizedExperiment with 1024 rows and 646039 columns
##  [6] fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048: SummarizedExperiment with 2048 rows and 646039 columns
## Functionality:
##  experiments() - obtain the ExperimentList instance
##  colData() - the primary/phenotype DataFrame
##  sampleMap() - the sample coordination DataFrame
##  `$`, `[`, `[[` - extract colData columns, subset, or experiment
##  *Format() - convert into a long or wide DataFrame
##  assays() - convert ExperimentList to a SimpleList of matrices
##  exportClass() - save data to flat files

2.1 Dataset version

Dataset HDD_v3.2, version 3.2.0.

The walkthrough reads the saved HDD object. See the results inventory for the companion exports. ADAPT agents-of-interest coverage was not assessed in this report.

2.2 Basic access examples

The examples below show the intended access pattern for release metadata, compound annotations, one assay matrix, and a small analysis-ready table. They operate on the object already loaded by this report and do not query a live service.

# Compound metadata
compound_metadata_example <- as.data.frame(colData(hdd_mae)) |>
  select(
    HDD.Compound.ID,
    Molecule.Name,
    Pubchem.CID,
    ChEMBL.ID,
    In.AnnotationDB
  ) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
compound_metadata_example
# One assay and a compact joined summary
tox21_matrix <- assay(experiments(hdd_mae)[["Tox21"]])
tox21_matrix[1:min(5, nrow(tox21_matrix)), 1:min(6, ncol(tox21_matrix))]
tox21_analysis_ready <- tibble::tibble(
  HDD.Compound.ID = colnames(tox21_matrix),
  measured_assays = colSums(!is.na(tox21_matrix)),
  positive_assays = colSums(tox21_matrix == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
) |>
  left_join(
    as.data.frame(colData(hdd_mae)) |>
      select(HDD.Compound.ID, Molecule.Name, Pubchem.CID),
    by = "HDD.Compound.ID"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(positive_assays), HDD.Compound.ID) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)
tox21_analysis_ready

4.1 DailyMed labels

DailyMed adds boxed warnings, warnings/precautions and adverse reactions to compound metadata. Labels are matched by exact PubChem CID and retain the selected label identifier, version and publication date.

1,750 compounds with a returned label
Field Populated Missing (null) Empty text
Boxed warning 559 1191 0
Warnings / precautions 1727 21 2
Adverse reactions 1695 55 0

Across HDD, 436,748 compounds were found in AnnotationDB without a label, 104,222 compounds with CIDs were not returned, and 105,402 compounds have no PubChem CID. These outcomes differ from a returned label with a missing or empty section. Missing text does not establish that a warning is absent.

The 1,750 compound annotations represent 1,432 distinct label-set/version pairs; 308 are shared across CIDs. AnnotationDB selected one label per compound, with multiple candidates reported for 1,167 compounds. These selections are not exhaustive and may be formulation-specific or historical. The plot counts each selected label-set/version once; the median publication date is 2026-04-04.

The examples below show annotated compounds and short label excerpts. Expand a row to view its text. Full sections remain in colData; excerpts are shortened only for display. Source text is retained verbatim; consult the source label for unreadable passages.

4.2 Long-form drug indications

Drug indication records are one-to-many with compounds and therefore remain a long table in metadata(hdd_mae)$Drug.Indications. This preserves repeated compound–indication associations in the data.

4.2.1 Clinical annotation coverage and ontology mappings

These annotations describe compound–indication associations, not a single clinical status assigned to each compound. MeSH identifiers and headings are retained alongside the source’s EFO.ID and EFO.Term fields. Despite that field name, the identifiers can belong to EFO, MONDO, HP, or other namespaces; the table below reports the prefixes actually present rather than assuming every mapping is an EFO identifier. Counts of records, compounds, and source indications are distinct: a source indication can occur for multiple HDD IDs.

4.2.2 Indication-specific development phases

The distribution below uses Maximum.Indication.Phase exactly as supplied by AnnotationDB/ChEMBL, including fractional and negative source codes. It is the maximum phase recorded for the particular indication, not necessarily an active trial’s phase or the compound’s overall development status. No source codes are relabeled as regulatory approval claims. Bars count association records; a compound with several indications can contribute more than once.

5.3 Fingerprints (Morgan count fingerprints)

Count-based Morgan fingerprints generated from parseable SMILES using RDKit. Each fingerprint experiment is stored as a sparse matrix of feature counts with rows as fingerprint bins and columns as the HDD.Compound.ID values that produced a fingerprint. Compounds with missing or invalid SMILES remain in colData but are not columns in the fingerprint experiments.
